title: Pulled a Courtyard Gold Coin? Keep, Sell or Redeem It
summary: Pulled a graded gold coin from a Courtyard pack? How the 7-day buyback, Courtyard's marketplace and redemption work, and how to sell the coin on Pure.
body_markdown:
You have four options for a gold coin you pulled from a Courtyard pack: keep it in Courtyard's vault, accept Courtyard's buyback offer within 7 days of the reveal, list it on Courtyard's marketplace, or redeem it and have the coin shipped to you in its original PCGS or NGC slab. Once it's in your hands, it's yours to keep or to sell anywhere, including on Pure, where[certified classic gold coins](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/gold-coins) are listed and the bids and asks are public, no account needed.


Maybe it's a $5 Liberty or an Indian quarter eagle, sealed in a slab with a cert number on the label. Here's how each route works, with Courtyard's terms linked to its own help pages.


Pure isn't affiliated with Courtyard. Courtyard's terms in this post were checked against its help center on November 23, 2026.


## First, What You Own After the Rip


A real coin. Courtyard keeps the physical piece in its vault; the thing in your app is the ownership record, tied 1:1 to that one coin ([Courtyard's coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) , dated June 29, 2026). Every coin in the pack pools was graded and slabbed by one of the two big U.S. graders before it went in. For U.S. coins, the fair market value Courtyard assigns comes from historical auction comps.


That FMV number shows up again in a minute, because Courtyard's buyback is pegged to it.


### How to Look Up Your Coin's Cert Number


The cert number is printed on the slab's label, and Courtyard ties it to your digital coin. Type it into[PCGS Cert Verification](https://www.pcgs.com/cert) or[NGC's cert lookup](https://www.ngccoin.com/certlookup/) (whichever company graded it) to pull up the grader's own record: grade, date, denomination, plus the grader's population data. Anyone you sell to later can run the same lookup.

## Option 1: Leave It in Courtyard's Vault


You don't have to do anything. The coin sits in an[insured, climate-controlled vault Courtyard operates](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) , tracked by its cert number. Redeeming or listing it later is still on the table.


## Option 2: Courtyard's Buyback Offer (7-Day Window)


Every coin you pull comes with what Courtyard calls an "instant buyback": an offer to buy the coin back from you, good for 7 days after the reveal.[Courtyard bases the offer on fair market value and says it comes in below it, with the spread covering its operating costs: custody, authentication checks and marketplace infrastructure](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) . There's no single published rate in its help center (as of November 23, 2026), so the number to go by is the offer Courtyard shows you.


Accepting is optional. Courtyard's[coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) also says pulled coins can't be returned ("All sales are final"); skip the offer and the coin simply stays in your collection with the other three routes open.


### Moving the Money Out of Your Courtyard Balance


The buyback credit lands as USDC in your Courtyard balance ([terms](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/13854269-terms-of-service) ) and can be spent on Courtyard right away. Getting it to a bank is a separate, ID-verified step (identity verification comes before your first withdrawal) ([withdrawal guide](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/9201319-how-to-withdraw-your-balance) , dated August 29, 2026). U.S. options include ACH (same-day or the standard 2 to 3 business days), a Visa or Mastercard debit card, PayPal, Venmo, or USDC sent to your own Polygon wallet. Amex and Discover cards can't receive payouts.


## Option 3: List It on Courtyard's Marketplace


You set the price. Other users can buy it outright or send offers; the[coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) lists zero listing fees and shows recent sales on each coin's page, so there's something to price against. When it sells, the coin never leaves the vault. The buyer just takes over the ownership record.


Courtyard's[marketplace guide](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/11955240-a-guide-to-the-courtyard-marketplace) carries a warning worth taking literally: a listing priced too low by mistake can be bought the moment it goes up, and accepted offers are final.


## Option 4: Redeem It and Have the Coin Shipped to You


Redeeming pulls the coin out of the vault and sends it to you; the digital version is retired once it's redeemed. Before anything goes out, Courtyard verifies your identity and your ownership of the coin ([terms](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/13854269-terms-of-service) ).


### What Shipping It Home Costs


There's no flat fee to quote. Shipping is charged at cost on FedEx pricing, set by destination, weight and carrier ([shipping article](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/9513558-how-to-ship-your-physical-collectibles) ), with the total (taxes included) on screen before you confirm. One catch: it has to go on a credit or debit card, because the wallet balance can't pay for shipping ([payment article](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/11955290-how-can-i-pay-for-my-shipment) , dated April 3, 2026).


### How Long Redemption Takes


Up to 10 business days to process a request, per Courtyard's[general shipping article](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/9513558-how-to-ship-your-physical-collectibles) , which is written for every vaulted item and not coins in particular. After that it goes out FedEx from Courtyard's vault in Delaware. Tracking arrives by email and in the Redemptions Tracker.


### Check the Insurance Before You Confirm


[Courtyard insures each shipment up to $100 by default and lets you buy more coverage when you place the shipment, so match the coverage to your coin before you confirm.](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard)


### Does the Coin Stay in Its PCGS or NGC Slab?


Yes. Coins ship in their original slabs, untouched, which means the label and cert number you looked up are the ones that arrive. A cracked slab or a damaged box gets reported to support with photos so a claim can be opened ([coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) ).


Once the coin is in your hands, the next section walks through selling it on Pure, if that's the route you pick.


## Selling a Redeemed Coin on Pure


This part is about us, so read it knowing we run the marketplace. Pure is one more path once the coin is in your hands: a U.S.-only marketplace where buyers post bids, sellers post asks, and anyone can see both without an account. Opening an account means a document check of about 15 minutes. There's no minimum to sell.[How to sell on Pure](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-sell-on-pure-marketplace) walks through every screen.


### Find Your Coin's Page and Grade


Search the marketplace for your coin and open its product page for your grader (PCGS or NGC), then pick your grade on the page. The[$2.5 Liberty PCGS page](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/25-liberty-gold-quarter-eagle-pcgs-generic-date000049) , for example, runs from MS60 up to MS66. Most classic U.S. gold on Pure is listed by type, grader and grade (those pages say "Generic Date"), not by individual year. If your coin is a specific date, reach out to the Pure team before you list so it goes on the right page.


### Set Your Own Ask or Sell Into the Highest Bid


When someone already has a bid up for your coin at your grade, you can sell into it: the sale fills right away and the price locks at that bid. No bid yet, or not one you'd take? Post an ask at the price you want and a buyer can take it from the page. If you haven't read an order book before,[this walkthrough](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-read-an-order-book-beginners-guide) explains the bid and ask columns;[how the Pure marketplace works](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-the-pure-marketplace-works) covers the rest.


### Ship It With Pure's Insured Label


Once it sells, Pure gives you an insured shipping label at no extra cost. The coin comes to us, never straight to the buyer. We test every item ourselves before it ships to the buyer. For boxing it up, follow the[packing guide](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-properly-ship-your-items-to-pure) .


### Fees and Payout


Seller fees on Pure run from 0.5% to 1.5% of the sale, depending on the item and your quarterly selling volume; a first-time seller starts at the entry tier. The tier table is in[Pure selling tiers](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/pure-selling-tiers) , with worked examples in[selling fees and shipping costs](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/selling-fees-and-shipping-costs-on-pure) . Payout is automatic: it's sent by ACH or check about 3 business days after your coin checks in.


For more than one pull,[selling a coin collection](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-to-sell-a-coin-collection) covers sorting a pile before you list it.


## If You Want a Specific Coin, You Can Buy That Coin Directly


Maybe the coin you were hoping for was one particular piece (a Saint-Gaudens double eagle in MS63, say), and a pack was one route to it. A pack assigns a coin at random from a pool, with the odds shown before you buy. On Pure (U.S. only), you pick the exact coin and grade, and you can see its current asks before you buy. Taking the lowest ask fills the order right away, with no buyer marketplace fee on top. Certified classic gold is in the[gold coins section](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/gold-coins) ; the wider[numismatic coins](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/numismatic-coins) page is the next place to look.


## FAQ


### Can I Sell a Courtyard Coin Somewhere Other Than Courtyard?


Yes. Once you redeem it, it's an ordinary graded slab, and any buyer can look up the same cert number.


### How Long Do I Have to Accept a Courtyard Buyback?


7 days from the reveal. After it expires, listing on Courtyard's marketplace and redeeming are both still available.


### Does Courtyard Charge Fees to List a Coin?


Its[coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) lists 0% for marketplace listings. The older[marketplace guide](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/11955240-a-guide-to-the-courtyard-marketplace) (August 2025) goes further: no fee charged to either the buyer or the seller on a peer-to-peer sale.


### Does a Redeemed Courtyard Coin Come in Its Slab?


It does: the original one, untouched.


### How Much Does It Cost to Ship a Coin Out of Courtyard's Vault?


Courtyard doesn't post a flat number. It's FedEx pricing at cost, shown before you confirm and paid by card. When you redeem several, the[coin FAQ](https://help.courtyard.io/en/articles/15033475-coins-on-courtyard) says they may ship together to cut the cost, depending on declared value and destination.


### Can I Sell a PCGS or NGC Graded Gold Coin on Pure?


Yes, if you're in the U.S. and your coin has a product page on Pure. Any current bids for your coin and grade are visible without signing up; the account comes when you're ready to list.
